questions.question: Which technological advance in 1947 is linked to the onset of the Information Age?
options: The invention of the personal computer
The creation of the World Wide Web
The deployment of the T-carrier system
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'The onset of the Information Age has been linked to the development of the transistor in 1947.'
Incorrect. The article notes that digital communication became economical after the invention of the personal computer in the 1970s, not 1947.
Incorrect. Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989, not 1947.
Incorrect. AT&T deployed the T-carrier in 1962, not 1947.

questions.question: According to the United Nations Public Administration Network, what became the driving force of social evolution in the Information Age?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that internet communications became 'the driving force of social evolution' according to the United Nations Public Administration Network.
Incorrect. Analog electronics are mentioned as an older format replaced by digital compact discs, not as a driving force of social evolution.
Incorrect. Mechanical calculators appeared in the 1600s as earlier calculating devices, not as part of the Information Age's driving force.
Incorrect. Punch cards were an enabling technology of the Industrial Revolution era, not cited by the UN as the driving force of social evolution.

questions.question: What was one advantage of converting technology from analog to digital format during the digital revolution?
options: Copies could be made identical to the original
Signals could be transmitted without any hardware
Information could only be accessed locally
Digital media degraded more quickly than analog media
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that by converting to digital format, 'it became possible to make copies that were identical to the original.'
Incorrect. The article mentions repeating hardware was used to amplify digital signals, not that signals could be transmitted without hardware.
Incorrect. The article highlights the ability to 'access or distribute it remotely,' which is the opposite of local-only access.
Incorrect. The article describes digital copies as identical to the original, implying no degradation, unlike analog formats.

questions.question: Which device is described as the world's first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Konrad Zuse completed the Z3 in 1941, 'the world's first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer.'
Incorrect. The Harvard Mark I was completed in 1944 and was inspired by Babbage's designs, but is not called the first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer.
Incorrect. Charles Babbage proposed the Analytical Engine, but it was never successfully built.
Incorrect. The LEO was the first commercially available general-purpose computer, not the first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer.

questions.question: Who is generally credited with laying the foundations of digitalization in a 1948 article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Claude Shannon, a Bell Labs mathematician, 'is generally credited with laying the foundations of digitalization in his pioneering 1948 article, A Mathematical Theory of Communication.'
Incorrect. John Bardeen co-invented the transistor in 1947, but is not credited with laying the foundations of digitalization in a 1948 article.
Incorrect. Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.
Incorrect. Robert Noyce invented the monolithic integrated circuit chip in 1959.

questions.question: What was the first commercially available general-purpose computer mentioned in the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the LEO was 'the first commercially available general-purpose computer.'
Incorrect. The Z3 was the world's first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer, but not the first commercially available general-purpose computer.
Incorrect. The Harvard Mark I was completed in 1944 and was inspired by Babbage's designs, but is not identified as the first commercially available general-purpose computer.
Incorrect. The Intel 4004 was the first single-chip microprocessor, released in 1971.

questions.question: What percentage of U.S. households owned a personal computer in 1984 according to the U.S. Census Bureau?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the U.S. Census Bureau's first survey showed that 8.2% of all U.S. households owned a personal computer in 1984.
Incorrect. 15.3% was the percentage of households with children under 18 that owned a computer in 1984, not all households.
Incorrect. 22.9% was the percentage of middle and upper middle class households that owned a computer in 1984.
Incorrect. 15% was the percentage of all U.S. households that owned a computer by 1989, not 1984.

questions.question: When were digital cell phones first sold commercially?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that digital cell phones were not sold commercially until 1991, when the 2G network started to be opened in Finland.
Incorrect. 1983 was when Motorola created the first mobile phone, the DynaTac, which used analog communication.
Incorrect. 1989 is not mentioned as the year digital cell phones were first sold commercially.
Incorrect. 1994 is mentioned as the end year for Commodore 64 sales estimates, not for digital cell phone commercial availability.

questions.question: Which company's CAPS system was used for animation films between 1990 and 2004?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Disney's CAPS system was used for all their animation films between 1990's The Rescuers Down Under and 2004's Home on the Range.
Incorrect. Apple is mentioned as an early personal computer manufacturer, not as the creator of the CAPS animation system.
Incorrect. Commodore is mentioned as an early personal computer manufacturer, not as the creator of the CAPS animation system.
Incorrect. Tandy is mentioned as an early personal computer manufacturer, not as the creator of the CAPS animation system.

questions.question: What did the change from analog to digitally recorded music during the 1980s illustrate about the digital revolution?
options: It was a turning point in the revolution
It proved analog sound was superior to digital sound
It decreased the ability to distribute music remotely
It made copying music more difficult
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'One turning point of the revolution was the change from analog to digitally recorded music.'
Incorrect. The article does not claim analog sound was superior; it describes digital formats replacing analog ones.
Incorrect. The article emphasizes the ability to 'access or distribute it remotely' as an advantage of digital information.
Incorrect. The article states digital format made it possible to make copies identical to the original, implying copying became easier, not more difficult.
